title: CAMPAIGN PROMISE
body:
Build the complete search system in Days 1–7. From Day 8, submit a precise daily quota, contact decision-makers, publish proof of expertise, and measure every result. Volume never excuses inaccuracy.

VERSION 1.0  •  AUGUST 2026

title: READ THIS FIRST
body:
How the campaign works
The rules that keep 1,000 applications useful, ethical, and measurable.

title: What counts as an application
body:
Count only a completed submission to one specific, open role. Creating a profile, joining a talent pool, sending a message, or bookmarking a vacancy does not count.
Never count duplicates. A role submitted through a board and again through the company ATS is still one application.
Apply only if the role accepts candidates based in Argentina and you meet roughly 60% or more of the real requirements.
No fabricated skills, dates, titles, employers, scope, or metrics. Every claim must be defensible in an interview.
If a scheduled portal has no valid vacancy, move that slot to a direct company ATS in the same market and record the substitution.
Tailor one priority Argentina application and one priority international application every day. The remaining applications use the closest approved role-family CV.

title: Operating assumptions and safeguards
body:
This is a demanding seven-days-a-week plan. Budget about 6–8 focused hours on application days and 7–9 hours during the build sprint. Batch research and content outlines to protect quality.
A second full-time role must be legally and operationally compatible with the current job. Check exclusivity, outside-employment approval, IP assignment, non-compete, schedule overlap, on-call duties, confidentiality, monitoring, and termination clauses before accepting.
Do not mislead either employer. Where policy or contract requires disclosure or permission, obtain it before starting. Never reuse confidential information, code, documents, client names, or equipment.
Never pay to apply, share banking credentials during screening, install unknown software, or continue when a recruiter cannot verify the company and role.
Daily content must be fact-checked and anonymized. Do not publish proprietary architecture, internal incidents, private team information, or unsupported achievements.
If one day is missed, distribute the deficit across the next seven days. The tracker recalculates the required pace; do not submit low-fit applications merely to restore the counter.

title: Candidate and AI copilot responsibilities
body:
Candidate owns
AI copilot supports
Truth, approvals, final edits, account logins, submissions, messages, publishing, interviews, legal/contract decisions.
JD ranking, ATS keyword comparison, drafts, CV tailoring, cover letters, outreach variants, blog editing, interview practice, tracker analysis.
AI support happens during active working sessions after the candidate provides the relevant job description, facts, and files; it is not an autonomous promise to act on future days.

title: Definition of a completed day
body:
The exact application quota is submitted and logged with working links, source, market, CV version, and next follow-up date.
Four new outreach messages and four follow-ups are sent on application days; one referral request is sent every second application day.
The daily article is published, its link is posted on LinkedIn and X, and the Instagram Story checkbox is completed manually.
Every status change and reply is recorded before the day is closed. The next day begins from the tracker, not from memory.

title: NEGOTIATION RULE
body: Do not volunteer the minimum. Ask: “What compensation range has been approved for this role?” If pressed, state a target range based on scope, employment type, benefits, currency risk, and schedule—not the lowest acceptable number.

title: PRODUCT SPECIFICATION
body:
The four-tab campaign platform
A simple single-user PHP/MySQL tool for the plan, assets, interview answers, applications, and daily content.

title: NAVIGATION DECISION
body: The platform has exactly four primary tabs: Plan, Kit, HR FAQ, and Tracker. Daily content lives inside each Plan day, so no additional Content tab is required.

title: FIXED TECHNOLOGY SCOPE
body: Use PHP, MySQL, Bootstrap, HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript only. Pages are rendered by PHP and standard HTML forms write directly to MySQL. There is no API, authentication, JavaScript framework, PHP framework, Node.js build process, cloud service, or external application dependency.

title: 1. Plan
body:
Header dashboard: current day, planned/actual applications, cumulative total, remaining to 1,000, Argentina/international split, content streak, replies, interviews, and offers.
Day navigator: Day 1–100 cards with status (Not started, In progress, Done, Blocked, Missed) and a fast jump to Today.
Daily workspace: outcome, candidate tasks, AI-copilot tasks, exact source/count table, outreach checklist, follow-ups, referral requirement, and definition of done.
Content panel: blog title, core angle, outline, article URL, ready X copy, ready LinkedIn copy, Instagram Story manual checkbox, publish timestamps, and channel links.
Evidence: links to submitted applications, tracker records, generated assets, published content, notes, blockers, and carry-forward actions.

title: 2. Kit
body:
CV library: 12 content versions and 36 exports; filters for language, family, format, status, last review, and supported keywords.
Templates: cover letters, application notes, recruiter messages, CTO/CEO messages, hiring-manager messages, referral asks, follow-ups, thank-you notes, salary scripts, and availability/contract questions.
Evidence bank: career facts, quantified accomplishments, project summaries, public links, technology inventory, approved stories, references, and red-flag claims requiring verification.
Version control: semantic name, version number, local file path, PDF, plain-text preview, change notes, and “approved for use” switch. Store file metadata in MySQL and the files in a local application folder. Never overwrite the master truth source silently.

title: 3. HR FAQ
body:
A bilingual searchable database of 150 classic HR questions with generic reusable answers—not a personal STAR-story database.
Fields: English question, Spanish question, generic English answer, generic Spanish answer, category, what the interviewer evaluates, what to avoid, personalization placeholders, likely follow-ups, difficulty, confidence, favorite, and last practiced.
Modes: browse, bilingual side-by-side, flashcard, random practice, timed mock interview, favorites, low-confidence review, printable view, and CSV export.
Categories: introduction, career history, strengths/weaknesses, motivation, company fit, teamwork, conflict, leadership, failure, remote work, time management, salary, availability, career changes, ethics, and closing questions.

title: 4. Tracker
body:
Table and Kanban views. Fields: company, role, market, platform, discovery source, canonical job URL, location eligibility, role family, CV, cover letter, salary/rate, application date, contact, follow-up date, stage, interviews, result, and notes.
Duplicate prevention: normalize company + title + canonical URL; warn before saving a second application to the same role.
Pipeline: Discovered → Selected → Preparing → Applied → Follow-up → Recruiter Screen → Technical → Leadership → Final → Offer → Accepted; alternate endings Rejected or Closed.
Analytics: response, screen, interview, final, and offer rates; conversion by market, portal, role family, CV version, recruiter, and week; median time to reply; overdue follow-ups; reasons for rejection.
Imports/exports: CSV; printable weekly report; MySQL backup. Do not store job-board passwords, banking information, identity documents, or current-employer confidential material.

title: NO-AUTH DEPLOYMENT BOUNDARY
body: Because the platform has no authentication, do not expose it directly to the public internet. Run it on localhost or a trusted private network. If public access ever becomes necessary, authentication must be added before deployment; that is outside this version’s scope.

title: MVP acceptance criteria
body:
All 100 days load with their exact quotas, source allocations, tasks, blog titles, X copy, LinkedIn copy, and Instagram checkbox.
Every screen is a PHP page using shared header, navigation, footer, database, validation, and message includes.
The Kit opens or downloads the correct approved local CV and prevents accidental use of an unapproved draft.
HR FAQ searches both languages and runs a JavaScript-assisted practice session while PHP/MySQL performs every save.
Tracker prevents duplicates with MySQL constraints, calculates all totals correctly, and shows 500/500 market progress.
A completed application is saved by a standard PHP POST form and updates both the day counter and dashboard exactly once.
The Bootstrap interface works on mobile, uses explicit Save actions, timestamps changes in Buenos Aires time, and supports mysqldump/CSV backup.
There are no API endpoints, login screens, user tables, tokens, sessions, external services, or framework/build dependencies.
No credential or confidential-employer data is collected. Basic accessibility: keyboard navigation, visible focus, labels, contrast, and non-color status indicators.

title: DAILY EXECUTION
body:
Day 1 through Day 100
Build for seven days. Apply for ninety-three. Publish and distribute one useful article every day.

title: DAILY ORDER
body: Open the Plan tab → process replies and due follow-ups → source and validate roles → tailor priority applications → submit and log → send outreach → complete the special focus → publish the article and social posts → close the day with evidence.
